# Updates, reaction, lineup, contract

Source: https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/live/lebron-james-signs-philadelphia-76ers-contract-salary-roster-updates-reaction-20260724.html

Skip to content
LeBron James’ signing adds an exclamation point to Sixers’ transformational summer
LeBron James’ Friday morning news dump did not come via ESPN television special or Sports Illustrated open letter.
Or on his agent’s podcast, for that matter.
Instead, it was one tweet from ESPN newsbreaker Shams Charania. And another from James’ agency, Klutch Sports, with confirmation. Then a thread of tweets from LeBron himself, with an initial explanation of what he is calling his final decision.
Show more
'It's a Philly King': Inquirer and Daily News front (and back) pages
Steve Gansey says Sixers fans are showing him the love after his brother's big move
Steve Gansey was at work on Friday morning when the texts started to trickle in.
Two colleagues from Philadelphia shared the news that LeBron James had signed with the 76ers. Gansey, the younger brother of new Sixers’ president of basketball operations Mike Gansey, logged onto Twitter/X, and saw a post from ESPN insider Shams Charania saying the same.
Like any other responsible basketball fan, he checked to make sure it wasn’t a prank account, before getting too excited.
Show more
Sixers preseason tickets prices are how much?!
We still don't know when LeBron James will make his regular-season 76ers debut, as the NBA has yet to drop its schedule, but two preseason games have already been revealed. And if you hope to see him in preseason action at Xfinity Mobile Arena, get ready to pay a pretty penny.
As of Friday afternoon, tickets for the Sixers' preseason home game vs. the Boston Celtics (7 p.m. on Oct. 16) start at $305 each for two tickets, according to
Vivid Seats
. A single ticket is $321. Tickets for the Sixers' other known preseason game, at the Celtics' TD Garden Oct. 10 (8 p.m.), start at $157 for two tickets together, while a single seat starts at $193.
We'll say it again: These are for
preseason
games.

Bryce Harper thinks LeBron picked 'a really good spot'
Long before
Bryce Harper
and LeBron James were Philly athletes, they each graced the cover of Sports Illustrated under the headline, "The Chosen One."
Now, Harper, who also picked Philly over other options in free agency, finds himself welcoming James to Philly.
—
Matt Mullin
Breaking down LeBron's decision to join the Sixers
'That's cheating': Kendrick Perkins, Vince Carter on LeBron signing
ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins, who played with LeBron James on the 2014-15 Cavaliers team that fell in the finals, said the future Hall of Famer's decision to sign with the Sixers made Philly a legitimate championship threat.
With an existing core of
Joel Embiid
,
Tyrese Maxey
,
VJ Edgecombe
, and the recently acquired Jaylen Brown, Perkins believes James is the piece that will put Philly over the top.
“The Philadelphia 76ers, with LeBron James, can win the championship this year, with this roster,” Perkins said. “The teams that he won a championship with, they had dogs… this is what [the 76ers] have”
Show more
M Night Shyamalan mocked over AI LeBron James image
In 2017, coming off the opening weekend of his film
Split
, M. Night Shayamalan rang the Sixers' ceremonial bell before the Philly team took on the LA Clippers. His daughter Saleka sang the national anthem.
"I can still remember when Dr. J retired," the filmmaker and die-hard Sixers fan who grew up in
Wynnewood
and lives in Willistown Township, wrote on the
Sixers website in 2019
. "It was a tough, tough night in the Shyamalan household."
A big fan of the late 1990s, Pat Croce, Allen Iverson, Dikembe Mutombo era, Shyamalan chose to celebrate LeBron James' decision to join the Sixers with
an AI generated image
of him and James, which he shared on Instagram. In it, the filmmaker is dressed in an armor embossed with the Sixers' logo and wears a metal crown. Next to him, James wears a "Phila 6" basket ball jersey and a crown more regal than Shyamalan's. Behind them, a chessboard serves as a background; Shayamalan is the knight (get it?) and James the king. The minimalist caption just tags James and the Sixers' Instagram accounts.
Show more
Sixers remain silent about LeBron, but not season ticket sales
The 76ers have not posted about LeBron James' decision to sign with the team on social media yet. However, it seems that the team's ticket sales department is looking to take advantage of the frenzy following the initial news breaking.
In a well-timed time message, the team sent out a reminder to past ticket purchasers that "2026-27 Season Tickets are selling out fast." Wonder why that may be?
—
Conor Smith
No plan for Bronny James to join LeBron in Philly: ESPN
'I was ready to cry' says one Sixers fans
Raymond Davis took the train into 30th Street Station to play basketball at Schuylkill River Park. Before leaving his home in Mount Airy, he put on his Tyrese Maxey to hoop in — not knowing LeBron James would sign with his favorite team shortly after.
“I didn't even know he was coming until I got on the train,” Davis said. “I was ready to cry on that jawn, bro. It’s so crazy. We getting the chip though, you know what I’m saying. This is the best our team ever looked and I’m just happy to be here. Happy for LeBron, been a LeBron fan since I was a young boul. It’s thorough.”
Davis met up with a few friends on the way to Schuylkill River Park. One of them, Christopher Gaines, is just as excited as Davis. Gaines is ready to write the day down in history books.
Show more
'We were picked!': Sixers fans react to LeBron signing
After LeBron James announced his decision, Lydia Victor and her sister bought a Whole Foods chantilly cake to celebrate. The Northeast Philly graphic designer and sports content creator had the bakery write “Trust the Process 23” in red frosting on top. She planned to cut it later Friday with her father, who went to college in Ohio and is the biggest LeBron fan, she said.
She said it almost didn’t matter if the James-led team wins a championship — though she was already planning to celebrate on Broad Street. The fact that James chose Philadelphia brought her more happiness than a championship (or potentially getting married or having kids) might. She likened the moment to Meredith Grey’s iconic monologue in the TV show
Grey’s Anatomy
imploring Derek Shepherd to choose her.
“It’s just the mindset that Philly isn’t always considered a big market and the national media usually counts us out when it comes to acquiring big name free agents,” she said. But this time, things were different.

LeBron James Sixers jerseys already sold out
Fanatics is already sold out of some LeBron James Sixers jerseys.
About two hours after the news broke, all first editions of the no. 23 jerseys
were sold out
on the Fanatics website. The adult royal blue, white, and red Swingman premium jerseys had been
selling for $124.99
, in line with the price of similar jerseys for other Sixers stars. Youth jerseys had also been available to pre-order for $69.99.
Red-and-blue adult Fast Break jerseys, which are made of different material, were available to preorder for $79.99 as of Friday afternoon. They were set to ship in early August.

Matt Cord offers up his LeBron James intro
Longtime Sixers public address announcer Matt Cord
retired at the end of the season
, but took a minute to offer up what his LeBron James intro would sound like during an appearance on 97.5 The Fanatic Friday.

Will LeBron claim his Honeygrow for life offer?
Honeygrow, the Philly-founded
fast casual food business
, tried to lure LeBron James to the Sixers in the day leading up to the announcement.
On Thursday, the company known for its made-to-order stir-fries as well as salads
posted on its Instagram
what sounded like an enticing offer: Come to Philadelphia, and we’ll give you free Honeygrow food for life, the company touted.
“Thoughts on taking your talents to Broad Street?” the company said in the Instagram post. “We’ve got all the Heat you need.”

Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe react to LeBron James coming to Philly
Philly’s other pro athletes are among the most excited about James coming to Philly, after big names like Bryce Harper and
Cooper DeJean
attempted to make their pitch on the All-Star red carpet.
Despite speculation that Jaylen Brown and James might have beef, after Brown said a few years ago that he didn’t believe James’ son Bronny was a pro, Brown was the first to post after the announcement.
Tyrese Maxey followed shortly after, posting a video of himself screaming in celebration at the gym.

Sixers' title odds skyrocket after LeBron news
A lot changed for the Sixers on Friday, including their title odds after LeBron James announced he'd be ending his free agency by signing with the Sixers.
Prior to James becoming a Sixer, they were listed as +2000 to win the NBA Finals, according to Sports Illustrated on July 20.
Philly is now up to +1000, the fourth favorite behind the Oklahoma City Thunder (+260), San Antonio Spurs (+260), and New York Knicks (+900).

Gov. Shapiro declares it 'LeBron James Day'
Gov.
Josh Shapiro
announced that Friday would be known as LeBron James Day in a proclamation posted on X following the announcement that the famed player would be signing with the 76ers.
“Pennsylvania is honored to welcome LeBron James to our Commonwealth as he joins the Philadelphia 76ers for his best season yet,” the proclamation reads.
Shapiro highlighted James’s record-breaking NBA career and philanthropic endeavors throughout the proclamation as a reason to dedicate the day to him.

LeBron explains why he picked the Sixers
Shortly after news broke that LeBron James planned on signing a two-year deal with the Sixers, the future Hall of Famer
took to social media
to explain his most recent decision. Here's the full text:
"I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game. I still truly love this game, and I have more to give.
"The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out. This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point?

Sielski: LeBron's arrival changes everything
Steph Curry changed the way basketball was played and the way boys and girls around the world wanted to play it, and among the fraternity of NBA players themselves, Kobe Bryant was more respected and feared, for his preparation and cutthroat competitiveness. But LeBron James has been greater longer than any other player in the sport (with the possible exception of Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, if you count his Lew Alcindor/UCLA years).
Set aside, if possible, the four NBA championships and the 10 Finals appearances and the league’s career scoring record and the three Olympic gold medals and the other records he has set. His choreographed announcement in 2010 that he was leaving the Cleveland Cavaliers for the Miami Heat was the 21st century’s answer to the revelation that Kristin Shepard had pumped two bullets into J.R. Ewing’s belly. It changed everything about the power that elite players held over their respective teams because it showed elite players that they held power over their respective teams. Pro sports hasn’t been the same.
Finding an athlete comparable to James in popularity and influence is difficult enough, let alone one who arrived in Philadelphia during the middle stage or latter half of his career, after he had established his galactic superstardom. Wilt Chamberlain already had been a high school phenom here when the Warriors made him a territorial pick in the 1959 NBA draft. Julius Erving was the “Babe Ruth of basketball” — at least, that’s how Sixers general manager Pat Williams described him in trying to persuade owner Fitz Dixon to cough up the money to acquire Dr. J. But Erving had spent six years in the relative obscurity of the ABA; telling someone you had seen him play for the Virginia Squires or New York Nets, whether in person or on TV, was akin to claiming you had spotted a Sasquatch.

When will LeBron make his Sixers debut?
Right now, we're still waiting for the NBA to release the Sixers' full 2026-27 schedule, but on Monday some preseason games began to trickle out, including a pair against the Boston Celtics on Oct. 10 (away, 8 p.m.) and Oct. 16 (home, 7 p.m.). Both games will likely air on NBC Sports Philadelphia, but could be promoted to a national network.
And that's assuming James even plays in the preseason.
At 41, James could opt to wait until the regular season opener to make his Sixers debut, although he has played in recent years, with the exception of last season when he also missed the first 14 regular-season games with sciatica.

Mike Gansey first earned LeBron's respect as a player
By now you've probably seen the picture. It was taken in 2000, and was on the front page of the Cleveland Plain Dealer’s sports section. Ten high school basketball players from Northeast Ohio stood side by side, in their respective jerseys.
The group had been voted by coaches and athletics directors as the best players in the region. There was Maverick Carter and Chester Mason (“Chet the Jet”) toward the left. Brian Swift was closer to the middle, alongside Mike Patrick.
But what caught everyone's attention was to the far right: future Sixers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey, of Olmsted Falls High School, alongside future Hall of Famer LeBron James, of St. Vincent-St. Mary.

LeBron's path to the Sixers was full of hints
From the asterisk next to Tyrese Maxey's name on Rich Paul's white board to LeBron James saying he wants to "trust the process" — and from Steve Gansey's viral picture to Tyrese Haliburton asking James if this was his 76th season — there have been no shortage of Easter eggs pointing to King James ultimately signing with the Sixers.
Were some of them random coincidences? Sure. Were some chum in the water for Sixers fans starving for a title? You bet. We may never know which was which, but you can recap it all — and see how each moment impacted his chances of ending up in Philly — with our patented Bron-O-Meter.

Sixers land LeBron and shock the NBA world
The 76ers had already shocked the NBA by acquiring Jaylen Brown in a blockbuster trade on July 2. They just one-upped themselves.
LeBron James, a legendary player and one of the most famous humans on planet Earth,
is coming to Philly
. According to ESPN, he agreed to a two-year contract with the Sixers on Friday in one of the more improbable roster additions in franchise history.
The second monumental move in a month further illustrates that the Sixers are making the all-in push toward championship contention in the Eastern Conference, joining a Toronto Raptors team that has reacquired Kawhi Leonard and a Miami Heat team that traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo in recent days.
